newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan mulls checks on foreign firms' mergers.
newsitem.headline: Japan mulls checks on foreign firms' mergers.

text.p: Japan's fair trade watchdog, worried that Tokyo alone among major economic powers lacks authority to check foreign mergers for domestic fallout, is considering changes to its own anti-monopoly law.
"We are studying the issue," Keiko Unotoro, director of the merger and acquisitions division of Japan's Fair Trade Commission (JFTC), told Reuters on Monday.

"The United States and the European Union are able to examine mergers by Japanese firms, so we question whether it is right for us to lack similar authority (with regard to foreign mergers)," she said.

A trans-Atlantic battle between Washington and Brussels over the merger of Boeing Co and McDonnell Douglas Corp nearly ignited a trade war before a face-saving compromise last week allowed both Boeing and Europe to claim victory.

The row -- and prospects of future scuffles among anti-trust authorities -- prompted EU Trade Commissioner Sir Leon Brittan to revive a call for negotiations for broad international standards to govern foreign scrutiny of mergers.
Such global standards are at present lacking despite the growing number of corporate marriages which affect markets outside the home countries of the firms involved.

The Geneva-based World Trade Organisation (WTO) last December set up a working group on anti-trust matters, but the United States is not ready for an international agreement which some fear would impinge on U.S. sovereignty.
The JFTC's Unotoro said Japan was not opposed to attempts to harmonise standards for foreign scrutiny of mergers, but added that the chances for success were cloudy.
"There have been efforts at harmonisation in such forums as the OECD (Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development) but it's been difficult," she said.

"My personal view is that it was only natural that the United States and the EU viewed the Boeing-McDonnell Douglas merger differently since each was looking at the impact of the merger on its own market," she added.

Unotoro said the JFTC was considering submitting revisions to allow examination of foreign mergers along with other revisions to the Anti-Monopoly Law to parliament during its next regular session from January, but was uncertain whether details could be worked out in time.
